extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary, secondary, postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, legal counsel, and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and regulatory requirements from the Department of Education's final Title IX rule describing recipients' obligations (definitions, grievance procedures, coordinator duties, pregnancy-related protections, scope of sex discrimination, retaliation, and administrative requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require fair, prompt, and equitable grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Require recipients to adopt grievance procedures that provide for fair, prompt, and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination and to take other necessary steps to provide an educational environment free from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grievance procedures must meet the specific procedural requirements set out in §§106.45 and 106.46 (and related preamble discussion). The Department strengthened obligations to provide prompt and equitable grievance procedures and to take other necessary steps when it receives a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "sex-based harassment"
rubrics_metrics.description: Define “sex-based harassment” as a form of sex discrimination that includes sexual harassment and harassment based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, or gender identity, that is quid pro quo harassment, hostile environment harassment, or one of four specific offenses referenced in the Clery Act (sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, stalking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations provide and clarify definitions of various terms related to a recipient's obligations to address sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify scope of sex discrimination (including sexual orientation & gender identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that sex discrimination includes discrimination on the basis of sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations explicitly apply Title IX's prohibition to these categories to ensure protections for students, teachers, and employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must designate a Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text clarifies administrative requirements with respect to designating a Title IX Coordinator and specifies Title IX Coordinator obligations including a duty to monitor (§106.44(b) and (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination policy, grievance procedures, and notice of nondiscrimination (§106.8(b) & (c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and disseminate a nondiscrimination policy, grievance procedures, and provide a notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These administrative requirements are clarified and streamlined; recipients must maintain and publicize these materials as part of their Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train a range of relevant persons on the recipient's obligations under Title IX, including training for decisionmakers under §106.46(f)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations specify who must be trained and identify training for decisionmakers as a topic in the Regulatory Impact Analysis; training is an explicit administrative obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records as required by the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping obligations are clarified; record retention and availability may be relevant to investigative and enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to operate programs free from sex discrimination (§106.44 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have an obligation to operate their education program or activity free from sex discrimination, taking action as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty includes multiple affirmative steps and monitoring obligations described in §106.44 and related subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers (§106.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must monitor for barriers that impede equal access or contribute to sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Title IX Coordinator obligations and recipients' duty to operate programs free from sex discrimination; appears in list of recipient actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with notification requirements when addressing sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification requirements are part of recipient duties under §106.44(c) and are separately listed in the Regulatory Impact Analysis as a cost/benefit consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee and confidentiality rules (sections 106.2 & 106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and set requirements for “confidential employee” status and related confidentiality protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain employees may be designated as confidential employees with limits on required reporting; definitions in §106.2 apply across the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness events (§106.44(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must consider or support public awareness events as part of prevention and response activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public awareness events are mentioned as one of the recipient actions to operate free from sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator requirements (detailed under §106.44(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific duties and responsibilities for Title IX Coordinators, including monitoring and providing information and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes duty to monitor, duties related to notification and supportive measures, and administrative responsibilities discussed in preamble and regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: provision and definition (§106.44(g) and §106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide supportive measures and follow the definition and procedural rules for supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes a range of supportive measures, requirements for provision, and an impartial review requirement (§106.44(g)(4)). The Regulatory Impact Analysis lists 'Provision of Supportive Measures' and 'Impartial Review of Supportive Measures.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may impose emergency removals when necessary to address threats to safety or education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removal procedures are subject to constraints and must be balanced with due process protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative leave (§106.44(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may place employees on administrative leave as part of response options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative leave is listed among possible recipient actions and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited disclosures of personally identifiable information (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are prohibited from making certain disclosures of personally identifiable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with FERPA and other privacy protections; disclosure limitations interact with investigative and notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution process (§106.44(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer an informal resolution process subject to regulatory limits and notice requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution is referenced both generally and specifically (see §106.46(j) for postsecondary student-involved cases). Consent and voluntariness and suitability considerations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework for grievance procedures — due process and procedural principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must adhere to due process principles, minimize administrative burdens, and allow recipients to respond to threats and promptly impose discipline while remaining consistent with other civil rights laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses general support, due process, administrative burdens, ability to respond to threats, quasi-judicial appearance concerns, and consistency with OCR enforcement of other civil rights statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability distinctions: elementary/secondary vs. postsecondary and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance framework addresses differences in application between elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions, and employee contexts (including possible bifurcation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subsections address elementary/secondary, employees, and postsecondary student-respondent/complainant contexts; bifurcation between students and employees at postsecondary institutions is a discussed point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can make a complaint (§106.45(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations detail who may file complaints of sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains definitions of party/complainant/respondent and clarifies that a parent/guardian/authorized representative may act on behalf of individuals (§106.6(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat complainants and respondents equitably throughout the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment is foundational and underlies procedural protections, access to supportive measures, and fairness in investigations and adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest or bias (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must address conflicts of interest and bias and provide for objective decisionmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble notes concerns about presumed guilt and emphasizes requirements to avoid bias or conflicts in investigators and decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that respondent is not responsible until determination (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a presumption that the respondent is not responsible until a determination is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption is explicitly required in the regulatory text to protect respondents' due process rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes for grievance procedures (§106.45(b)(4) and §106.46(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include timeframes for major stages of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeframe requirements appear in both general and postsecondary-specific provisions; the preamble discusses directed questions and public comment on timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable limitations on sharing information (§106.45(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures should contain reasonable limitations on sharing of information among parties and third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing privacy, FERPA, and the parties' rights is discussed; sharing limitations interact with access to relevant evidence provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and exclusion of impermissible evidence (§106.45(b)(6) & (7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations and decisionmaking must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence and exclude impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text and preamble discuss evaluating relevance, excluding hearsay or otherwise impermissible evidence, and how evidence review should proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allegations (§106.45(c) and §106.46(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide written notice of allegations to parties in accordance with regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For postsecondary cases, §106.46 delineates written notice requirements specific to student-involved complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of a complaint (§106.45(d) and §106.46(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations specify grounds and process for dismissing complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both general and postsecondary-specific dismissal provisions are addressed and discussed in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of complaints (§106.45(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations allow consolidation of complaints where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation rules must be included in grievance procedures and applied consistent with fairness and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint investigations and investigative burden (§106.45(f) and (f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must investigate complaints and bear investigative burdens as specified in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative burden language clarifies recipients' responsibilities to gather and evaluate relevant evidence; the preamble addresses concerns about presumption and investigative practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present witnesses and other evidence (§106.45(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have the opportunity to present witnesses and other evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should allow parties to present evidence consistent with rules on relevance and impermissible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.45(f)(4) and §106.46(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have access to evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postsecondary-specific provisions emphasize access to relevant evidence and detail procedural safeguards (e.g., advance notice of meetings, advisor role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating allegations and assessing credibility (§106.45(g) and §106.46(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require processes for evaluating allegations and assessing credibility of evidence and witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessing credibility should be done objectively with stated criteria; training for decisionmakers is linked to credibility assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof (§106.45(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations set or allow recipients to set a standard of proof for determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble references Directed Question 4 about standards of proof; §106.45(h)(1) addresses the standard to be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of determination whether sex discrimination occurred (§106.45(h)(2) and §106.46(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify parties of the determination whether sex discrimination (or sex-based harassment) occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications must comply with regulatory content and timing requirements; postsecondary hearings/live hearings provisions feed into final determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and prompt/effective steps (§106.45(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide remedies to a complainant and other appropriate prompt and effective steps following a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies must be appropriate, timely, and designed to restore or preserve equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply before imposition of disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(h)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with §106.45 procedural requirements before imposing disciplinary sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that disciplinary action is not imposed without following mandated grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discipline based solely on determination (§106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations prohibit imposing discipline based solely on a determination of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section interacts with retaliation protections and with appeals/process fairness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals (§106.45(i) and §106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must provide for appeals of determinations in accordance with regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be structured to preserve fairness and may address procedural or substantive errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of supportive measures and disciplinary sanctions and remedies (§106.45(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require grievance procedures to include a range of supportive measures, disciplinary sanctions, and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must list or describe possible measures and sanctions to allow transparency and appropriate responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary-specific procedural protections (§106.46): advisor role, advance notice, live hearings, expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: For sex-based harassment complaints involving a student complainant or respondent at postsecondary institutions, additional requirements include notice in advance of meetings, role of advisor, other persons present, expert witnesses, timeframes, access to evidence, evaluating allegations, live hearings, determinations, appeals, and informal resolution rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46 contains postsecondary-specific procedural rules including training for decisionmakers (§106.46(f)(4)) and live hearing provisions (§106.46(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary review (§106.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for Assistant Secretary review procedures as specified in §106.47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistant Secretary review is an administrative review mechanism described in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for pregnancy and parental status (§106.2; §§106.40 & 106.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define “pregnancy or related conditions” and “parental status” and clarify protections for students and employees on the basis of current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations define terms and detail obligations including responsibility to provide Title IX Coordinator contact information, reasonable modifications, voluntary leaves, lactation space, limitation on supporting documentation, and comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions and parental/family status protections (§106.21(c) and §106.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations prohibit discrimination in admissions based on parental, family, marital status, pregnancy, or related conditions and set related recipient responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific actions to prevent discrimination and ensure equal access for students and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee protections re pregnancy/parental status (§106.51(b)(6), §106.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect employees against discrimination based on parental/family/marital status, pregnancy, or related conditions and address granting and return from leaves, lactation time and space, and pre-employment inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employee-specific provisions mirror student protections and add employment-related processes and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis harm standard and participation consistent with gender identity (§106.10 & §106.31(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify that, except as permitted, recipients must not carry out different treatment or separation on the basis of sex in a way that would cause more than de minimis harm; include participation consistent with gender identity and other scope clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 106.31(a) outlines application, de minimis harm standard, participation consistent with gender identity, parental rights, intersections with health care and religious beliefs, appearance codes, juvenile justice facilities, and burden on schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibition (§106.71 and definitions in §106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibit retaliation; define protected activity, adverse action, causal connection, and peer retaliation, and provide examples of prohibited retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble discusses general support/opposition, intersection with §106.45(h)(5), First Amendment considerations, and requests to clarify or modify the retaliation text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory administrative requirements: transparency, coordination, data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and OCR must address transparency, coordination, data collection (including climate surveys), technical assistance, funding for compliance, and reporting as part of implementation and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miscellaneous items addressed in the preamble include transparency, funding, technical assistance, coordination, data collection and climate surveys, and OCR enforcement practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact and implementation timing (Effective date Aug 1, 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department sets effective date to allow recipients time to plan (effective August 1, 2024) and analyzes regulatory impacts including costs, benefits, small business impacts, and alternatives in the RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing reflects consideration of public comments on effective date and retroactivity; RIA sections discuss need for action, costs/benefits, accounting, and regulatory flexibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions apply across entire part (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions in §106.2 apply to the entirety of 34 CFR part 106 unless a provision specifically references otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble clarifies that references to definitions 'as defined in §106.2' provide extra clarity but the §106.2 definitions are generally binding across the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of rights and interaction with other laws (§106.6 & related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the effect of other statutory requirements (e.g., GEPA/FERPA) and preservation of rights, including exercise of rights by parents/guardians/authorized representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections discuss how Title IX regulations interact with FERPA and other statutes and preserve certain rights and procedural interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on supporting documentation for pregnancy-related accommodations (§106.40(b)(3)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the type/amount of supporting documentation required for pregnancy or related condition accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to reduce burdens on students and employees seeking accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions (pregnancy provisions §106.40 & §106.57(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancy or related conditions and lactation must be treated comparably to other temporary medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure similar access and modifications as would be provided for other temporary medical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary access to separate and comparable portions of programs (§106.40(b)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer voluntary access to a separate and comparable portion of a program/activity for pregnancy-related circumstances, subject to comparability and voluntariness standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such separations must be voluntary and comparable, and not result in more than de minimis harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-investigator model considerations (§106.45 discussion / RIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of concerns and regulatory treatment regarding single-investigator models for investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA and preamble note training, impartial review, and administrative burdens in relation to investigative models; the single-investigator model is specifically referenced.
